Sell Me Locke

STS-HS10-L4-13001400-HSWH-STP-EUR-01 • HS World History Grade 10 • Enlightenment Philosophers and Democratic Revolutions
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Three hundred years ago, people argued about who should hold power in the coffeehouses and salons of Europe, and the strongest ideas spread the way a good pitch spreads today. Tonight Klara, Henri, and Petra are selling those ideas as trading cards, and every card has to print what its thinker is actually worth. Locke's card sells natural rights. Montesquieu's card sells the idea that no single person should ever hold every power.
If you made a card for Rousseau, what one idea would you print on it?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Klara doing?
Look at the picture. Justify what Klara is doing with exact evidence. Use precise words, not “stuff.”
2
What is Henri holding?
Look at the picture. Justify what Henri holds and why he raises it. Name the object exactly.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Justify what the teacher is doing with exact evidence from the picture.
4
What room is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Justify what place this is with at least two exact clues.
5
Tell me about the pitch board.
Look at the picture. Justify how the pitch board presents the set of thinkers. Use exact terms.
6
What is Petra wearing?
Look at the picture. Justify Petra's role from her clothing and where she is sitting. Be precise.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: HSS 10.2.1 — Enlightenment philosophers and their influence on democratic revolutions in England, the United States, France, and Latin America. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
